paid_market_gaps.gap: Enterprise platforms sell via large annual commits (Pillar $175k, Lasso $20k+); small teams have few paid options besides Knostic.
Native agent permission rules are pattern-based; argument rules are bypassable by compound commands, pushing users to sandboxing.
Headless/non-interactive agent runs often auto-approve all tool calls, with no read-only or plan mode.
Per-call policy engines do not yet correlate sequences of individually allowed calls into malicious workflows.

market_research.wtp_evidence: Public prices exist: Pillar platform $175,000/12 months and Lasso for GenAI Chatbots $20,000 annual commit (12 months) on AWS Marketplace, Knostic Kirin $15/user/month.
market_research.bundling_note: Agent vendors ship free permission rules and managed deny settings (Claude Code), AWS meters Cedar tool-call policy in AgentCore, and Microsoft and Docker give away open-source MCP policy gateways.
market_research.summary: Crowded and consolidating (SentinelOne-Prompt, well-funded Pillar, Lasso, Runlayer) with free native and cloud controls. Narrow opening: cheap cross-agent policy enforcement for small and mid-size dev teams, including headless/CI agent runs, below enterprise annual commits.

threat.reason: Directly blocks prompt-injection-driven unsafe tool calls and exfiltration, an actively exploited agent attack path.

market_research.summary: Crowded and fast-bundling: funded gateways (Runlayer, MintMCP), identity incumbents (Auth0, Descope) and clouds (AWS, Cloudflare, Microsoft) all cover it. Only a narrow wedge remains, e.g. self-serve per-agent credentials and audit for mid-market teams across clouds.

threat.reason: Scoped agent credentials and tool-call audit limit token theft and misuse; MCP abuse still emerging, not yet common.

flagged_claims.claim: Vendor Pillar Security (Pillar for AI Coding Agents): discovers local coding agents, scans permissions/MCP configs; AWS Marketplace $175,000/12 months
flagged_claims.issue: The cited AWS listing describes the general Pillar Security Platform (AI apps, agents, MCP, red teaming, guardrails). It does not mention coding agents or local agent discovery. The $175,000/12 months is for the whole platform, not a coding-agent product.
